review_text_raw:
Pretty boring, to be honest. It feels so much like a bootleg version of Hacknet, except without the badass soundtracks and cool hacking features.


[b]/STORY and CHARACTERS (6/10)/[/b]

First things first, let's start with the story and characters. You're an agent from the government cyber security agency MI7 that investigates with other MI7 agents a group of hackers called Thorn who breached their servers. Your job is to track down all the members of the group and arrest them for a different crime in order to hide the security breach to the public. Alright, sounds simple enough, but that's because it IS simple, it's not more fleshed out than that. You spend the whole game hunting down an entire hacker group, then find an excuse to arrest them (I'll get back on that later). Even when you detain the big leader, none of what you've done felt satisfying after that.

As for the characters, well you don't have that much of character development from them, except for the "smart girl of the team" agent Sharp, the "bossy boss who takes his job way too seriously" Osvalt, the "I prefer old TTS softwares" agent on the field Cooper, the "flirty secretary who puts winky emojis all over her emails" Ashley, the "hahaha, I'm evil" hacker group leader Mr. Blue. Anyway, you get the point. Each character is only limited to one main characteristic and that's it.

[b]/GAMEPLAY (4/10)/[/b]

Oh boy, the gameplay is the main(lining) reason why I'm not recommending this. Jeez, where do I start? Well, first of all, if you're expecting to feel like a hacker, you're in for a disappointment. All you get is a command-prompt application with two script-kiddie commands: one that gets a website's IP and one that hacks into someone's computer using the said IP. That's right, throughout the whole game you'll spend most of your time typing 'ping', 'iphack', 'ping', 'iphack' while searching a computer's files in a DOS-style file navigation system. The devs claimed that it was on purpose in order to emphasize the narration over actual hacking. I would be fine with that kind of decision, but that doesn't mean you should stick to that repetitive "look at a website, ping, iphack and read files" bulls hit. At least keep an enjoyable gameplay in the background as well. Luckily, you get some other apps (like the google map one) and Operating Systems on the way.

On top of that, the arrest system is really nitpicky about which evidence you use against the person. Each case has around three alternate crimes to choose from to arrest the person you're tracking. However, only 1 evidence per crime is accepted code-wise. In other words, if you choose a proof that totally makes sense but wasn't chosen by the devs, it doesn't count. I ended up spamming the "begin arrest" button with every file I snatched.

As for the OS interfaces, it's a buggy mess, no matter which one is it. You start off with a parody Windows XP, which is pretty nice. You also get parody Ubuntu, parody Mac and parody Windows Vista/7 on the way, which is also great. The pixel art is pretty good, but the Operating Systems look so limited in comparison to the real thing, they don't feel like Operating Systems that anyone would actually use in real life (I know it's just a game, but come on). You can't delete files in your folder (too bad if you accidentally downloaded the same thing twice!) and the notepad doesn't save what you wrote into a text file, which is pretty inconvenient when I constantly need to write down IPs and names (and if you accidentally closed the notepad, too bad!). Also, if you keep windows open in Windows XP, then switch to another OS, open windows in that said OS, then switch back to Windows XP, the windows will start overlapping. I'm not impressed, man. Don't you have a "visible/invisible" property on your images or something in the engine you're using? Oh, and you're gonna love this one: the program is so delayed that if you type something way too fast, some keys will be ignored. Most of the time, you're going to have a lot of "mainlining" ending up like "manliin" because the game couldn't keep track of everything you typed down. This is super annoying when you type an IP, but get an error because the fucking game missed a keystroke and you don't know why it doesn't work since the error message doesn't tell you anything about what went wrong.

There are even reports of people who couldn't advance in some cases because the program forgot to add certain chat messages on the left to let you continue, which is frustrating when you can't even save in the middle of a case and instead start the whole thing over again. Luckily, I didn't encounter those case advancement bugs, but if you can't make a OS interface themed game with basic typing and windows manipulation without being overflowed with bugs, you shouldn't even sell it at 8-10 bucks. Personally, from my experience with this game, I think it should be five dollars at best, or even free.

[b]/CONCLUSION/[/b]

To conclude, I don't recommend this game. It's half-baked, it looks like a prototype game and doesn't have any satisfaction upon playing it whatsoever. The replayability value is somewhat there, but I put the game aside about two or three times before finally finishing it. If you feel like buying a hacking game without caring about anything else, then go for it. Otherwise, I'm giving this game...
